segment.description: The Hatchie River in West Tennessee as cataloged: the free-flowing bottomland swamp river running west through the Hardeman/Haywood corridor and on through Tipton and Lauderdale counties toward the Mississippi. Warmwater fishery (crappie/catfish/bass rules), no trout program.
segment.boundaries: Catalog covers the whole Tennessee river (hydroIdentity HUC8 08010208). TDEC scenic-river page: approximately 202.8 designated miles located in McNairy, Hardeman, Madison, Haywood, Tipton, and Lauderdale counties, designated February 12, 1970 as 'a swamp river' (Class I Natural River Area).

coldSource.notes: No dam tailwater: TDEC describes the Hatchie as 'the longest free-flowing tributary of the lower Mississippi River totaling 238 miles'. SpringFed=false basis: TDEC records its 1970 designation as 'a swamp river' — a rain/backwater-fed bottomland system, not a spring-fed stream; TDEC adds it 'provides habitat for more than 100 species of fish including 11 species of catfish' (warmwater-native assemblage, no trout mentioned). elevationFt = USGS gage altitude 266.99 ft (NGVD29) at HATCHIE RIVER NEAR STANTON, TN (07030000), identity verified via https://waterservices.usgs.gov/nwis/site/?sites=07030000&siteOutput=expanded&format=rdb and the statewide site file https://waterservices.usgs.gov/nwis/site/?format=rdb&stateCd=tn&siteOutput=expanded&siteStatus=all

holdover.detail: No trout fishery of any kind is documented on the Hatchie. The river is absent from TWRA's live trout stocking list (checked 2026-09-18) and from the TWRA Trout Management Plan 2017-2027 (zero mentions of 'Hatchie'); that plan states hatchery-supported waters 'are primarily warmwater habitats that cannot support trout year round'. Absence of a program is documented; absence of individual stocked fish was not surveyed.

wildPopulation.detail: No wild trout documented. TDEC's scenic-river page describes >100 native fish species including 11 catfish species with no trout; TWRA's Trout Management Plan contains no Hatchie reference.

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: Free-flowing warmwater swamp river: USGS grab samples at the Bolivar gage (07029500, 88 summer samples 1976-2005) peaked at 31.0 C in July 1986 and still hit 28.5 C in August 2005, and TWRA stocks no trout anywhere on the river.
